No alternative diagnosis explains the full constellation: placental abruption would more likely show uterine hyperstimulation/hypertonus and often greater hematocrit drop; vasa previa would present with painless bleeding and rapid fetal demise without maternal shock this early; uterine inversion is exceedingly rare and would show visible fundal depression and profound shock out of proportion to blood loss.
